_comment: Curated layer for the `surface` section of docs/capabilities.json (discoverability-design.md §1.2). NOTE the honest boundary: stapel-mailtrap's capabilities.json is otherwise still HAND-WRITTEN — this module has no schema/flows/errors emitter (see git log: 'author capabilities.json for the stapel-catalog sweep'), so provides/axes/extension_points/requires are not derived from code. `make contract` patches in the two derivable things: module/version from pyproject and the derived `surface`. NOTE what is deliberately NOT here: MailtrapEmailProvider (provider.py) is the sanctioned integration path for anything already wired through stapel-notifications' EMAIL_PROVIDER seam, and that seam is already named as an extension_point in capabilities.json — restating the class here would be the same prose twice. What IS here are the two entry points a host reaches for when it is NOT going through that seam: trap_email() for a custom mail backend that wants to plug into the trap directly (provider.py's own docstring says as much), and get_scope_provider()/purge_expired() for code that needs the same tenant-scoping or retention sweep the built-in views/command already use.

trap_email.intent: The single write path for capturing one outbound email as a TrappedEmail row, transactionally emitting mailtrap.email.trapped. Reach for this directly from a host's OWN mail-sending code path that does not go through stapel-notifications' EMAIL_PROVIDER seam (which already routes through this function via MailtrapEmailProvider) — do not hand-roll a second capture table or a bare logger.info() of outbound mail in dev/staging.

purge_expired.intent: The retention sweep (STAPEL_MAILTRAP['TTL_DAYS'] + ['MAX_EMAILS']) shared by the purge_trapped_emails management command and the Celery task. Call this directly when a host needs the sweep on its own schedule or trigger (an admin 'purge now' button, a different task queue) — it is the one place both limits are implemented, so a hand-written deletion query is one of the two casually forgotten.

get_scope_provider.intent: Resolve the configured STAPEL_MAILTRAP['SCOPE_PROVIDER'] instance — the same call TrappedEmailListView/TrappedEmailDetailView make before filtering. Reach for this from any host-written view or report over TrappedEmail so it stays subject to the same tenant scope as the built-in Mail API, instead of re-reading the setting and instantiating the provider by hand (which is exactly how one code path could end up unscoped while the others are not).
instead_of: re-reading STAPEL_MAILTRAP['SCOPE_PROVIDER'] and instantiating it by hand
